method: AI web verification (owner ruling 2026-11-06: AI-sourced URL+date suffices for entry; human-review gate retired). Coordinates, elevation, opening/illumination windows and seasonal windows verified per spot before contract authoring.
scope: CL-DATA-34: seven no-V2-contract jp legacy spots (jp-001, jp-012, jp-014, jp-015, jp-017, jp-018, jp-024). jp-037..049 and CL-DATA-32 additions (jp-051..064) excluded by ticket scope.

evidence.supports: Blue Pond coordinates 43.493583N 142.614028E (V1 point within ~15 m) and elevation ~500 m on the left bank of the Biei River; artificial pond of the 1989 Tokachidake lahar-control dams, drowned larches (karamatsu).
evidence.limitation: Community encyclopedia; coordinates cross-checked against V1 POI

evidence.supports: Biei Tourism Association (official): pond water from the aluminum-bearing Shirahige Falls / Biei River mix turns cobalt blue, drowned larches over a mirror surface; seasonal expressions.
HOKKAIDO LOVE! (official): autumn foliage contrasts with the blue water; calm-water reflections of the standing dead larches; bridge overlook.
evidence.limitation: No foliage dates given; window is climatological

evidence.supports: Kanagawa Prefecture official: Kotoku-in (Kamakura Daibutsu) hours 8:00-17:30 (Apr-Sep), 8:00-17:00 (Oct-Mar), open year-round.

Kotoku-in autumn foliage: ginkgo and maple peak 11-late to 12-early (info confirmed by the Kotoku-in temple office); maple trees behind the Great Buddha are the representative vantage; no illumination.
evidence.limitation: Commercial guide, but temple-office confirmed; window climatological

evidence.supports: Setagaya City (official): Todoroki Valley Park, ~1 km gorge carved by Yazawa River into the Musashino terrace, the only gorge in Tokyo 23 wards, designated scenic spot.
evidence.limitation: No elevation published; camera altitude left unknown

evidence.supports: Todoroki Valley autumn: both banks of the ~600 m boardwalk turn red, stream with falling leaves; local tourism portal.
evidence.limitation: No dates; Tokyo foliage window climatological

evidence.supports: Kokyo Gaien (Imperial Palace outer garden, Environment Ministry managed): plaza area open at all times, free, no regular holidays; classic Nijubashi photo point is the Seimon Stone Bridge view across the moat (stone bridge + iron bridge + Fushimi-yagura).
evidence.limitation: Special events/closures possible; hours guidance only

evidence.supports: Kenrokuen winter hours 10-16..2-end 8:00-17:00 (last entry 16:30); yukitsuri (snow-hanging rope work) starts 11-01, whole garden hung by mid-December; winter illumination 'Fuyu no Dan' 18:00-21:00 on ~8 February nights only (free, no reservations); yukitsuri reflected in Kasumiga-ike.
evidence.limitation: Secondary source quoting Ishikawa Prefecture official pages

evidence.supports: Kenrokuen yukitsuri typical viewing mid-December to late February; snow scene requires snowfall; Kenrokuen Park winter illumination event window.
Nagoya Castle official FAQ: the castle keep exterior is illuminated EVERY DAY from sunset until 23:00 (21:30 on the 8th of each month / green campaign nights may switch off earlier).
evidence.limitation: Illumination of the exterior; castle grounds close 16:30 so the night view is from the surrounding area

evidence.supports: Nagoya City official tourism: Nagoya Castle grounds 9:00-16:30, closed 17:00 (longer hours only during festival periods).
Osaka Castle official FAQ: keep illumination runs every day from sunset until 24:30, ramping up over ~1 h after sunset; only the one annual inspection day is dark.
Osaka Castle Park is free and the park itself is open 24 h (paid facilities have their own hours); the illuminated keep is viewed from around Gokuraku-bashi and the inner moat.
evidence.limitation: Secondary source; visit routes follow on-site notices

evidence.supports: Kotoku-in hours detail 8:00-17:30 (Apr-Sep) / 8:00-17:00 (Oct-Mar), last entry 15 min before closing, year-round; bronze Great Buddha height 13.35 m per the JNTO/enjoytokyo figure used for jp-012-P01 copy.
evidence.limitation: Secondary source cross-checked against the Kanagawa Prefecture official page (e-d34-d)
